stackedOn.state: OPEN at the time of this checkpoint
stackedOn.why: The dispatch requires the denominator to be DECLARED into SS-W12's capability rather than built as a fourth one-off scorer. registry.ts does not exist on main, so creating it here would have collided catastrophically with #438. The branch carries an explicit merge of ss/w12-scorer-harness: git records the dependency, #438 merges first, and this PR's diff then reduces to its own three commits. Stated rather than assumed, per the dispatch's instruction to say so.
stackedOn.risk: This PR's diff-vs-main carries 3,684 lines of another lane's code that is still under adversarial review. If the planner rejects part of #438, this PR carries it. Named as a review hazard rather than hidden.

heavyScanConfirmed.shape: 8 counties in one serialized psql loop, 5m25s wall clock; Travis 48453 run separately at 4m33s; Bastrop 48021 at 3.9s. One heavy scan at a time throughout. Read-only.
heavyScanConfirmed.note: ST_Subdivide on the city geometry is load-bearing, not tuning: without it the Travis query did not return inside a 2-minute budget. With it the parcel GiST index does the work.

whatWasBuilt.notAFourthScorer: No new scorer CLI, no new route, no migration. One new DenominatorKind, its measurement function, a per-county refusal rule, and one shared display-state module.

sixCausesNotOne.label: VERIFIED
sixCausesNotOne.claim: The denominator was the county parcel count, which charges a county for land no municipality can zone.
sixCausesNotOne.evidence: Bastrop 9,642/63,357 = 15.22% vs 9,526/11,968 = 79.60%. Only 18.89% of the county's parcels are inside an incorporated boundary.

sixCausesNotOne.label: VERIFIED
sixCausesNotOne.claim: The numerator escapes a naively-counted denominator, which is the mud 209/186 shape.
sixCausesNotOne.evidence: 116 stamped Bastrop parcels (1.20% of the numerator) and 16,308 Travis ones (5.9%) sit outside every municipal boundary; 65 of Bastrop's do not touch one, mostly elgin-tx R-1. Two independent counts give Bastrop 80.56%; the filtered rule gives 79.60%.
sixCausesNotOne.fix: Numerator is a FILTER on the denominator set inside one query, so num <= den holds by construction.

sixCausesNotOne.label: VERIFIED
sixCausesNotOne.claim: rule.denominator was DECLARED AND NEVER READ. measureColumnStamp called readParcelFeatureCount unconditionally, so the registry's required denominator field was documentation rather than control.
sixCausesNotOne.evidence: Read at source on ss/w12-scorer-harness b6909582: measureColumnStamp has no reference to rule.denominator. A rule could declare any denominator and get the parcel-feature count.
sixCausesNotOne.fix: denominatorNeedsCityBoundary is exhaustive over DenominatorKind with a `never` assignment, so adding a kind without deciding this is a type error.

sixCausesNotOne.label: VERIFIED
sixCausesNotOne.claim: SS-W13's per-county refusal never reached SS-W12's capability, because #438 was authored before #439 merged.
sixCausesNotOne.evidence: measureColumnStamp on the #438 branch has no wired-layer check. Run over county_manifest it would write zoning 0.00% not-yet for the 244 counties with no wired layer, which is exactly the defect SS-W13 merged a fix for one PR earlier.
sixCausesNotOne.fix: countyMeasurability.ts CALLS resolveStampFacetMeasurability. One authoritative copy (DEV_PROCESS 6.2); the engine already imports classifyFacet from the same file for the same reason.

sixCausesNotOne.label: VERIFIED
sixCausesNotOne.claim: Caldwell 48055 holds 26,155 parcel features with a PostGIS geom on ZERO of them, and it is not alone: 189 of the 253 counties holding parcels are in the same state.
sixCausesNotOne.evidence: SELECT per county over txgio_parcel: 48055 features=26155 with_geom=0; every other wired county 100.00%. Statewide: counties_with_parcels=253, counties_zero_geom=189, counties_partial_geom=0. Caldwell's jsonb geometry and bbox columns are both populated, so nothing about it looks empty; only the PostGIS column was never backfilled.
sixCausesNotOne.whyItMatters: A spatial denominator over Caldwell is silently zero while the store holds 6,527 stamped parcels. Refused with a basis naming the backfill, never scored.

sixCausesNotOne.label: VERIFIED
sixCausesNotOne.claim: The refusal ORDER was wrong on first write, and running the CLI caught it where reading the code had not.
sixCausesNotOne.evidence: With geometry checked before the instrument's reach, Anderson 48001 reported no-parcel-geometry. True, and it names work that would not make Anderson measurable, because it has no wired zoning layer either. At 189 zero-geom counties that would have published 189 spurious backfill items and buried the one county where geometry IS the binding constraint.
sixCausesNotOne.fix: Order is now no-parcels, then reach (SS-W13's three), then the denominator's own source, then geometry. Both directions pinned by tests.

WRITTEN layer (txgio_parcel + tx_city_boundary in the deployment store); no ledger figure used.
nineWiredCountiesMeasured.threshold: 95.00 (COUNTY_RAIL_DECLARATION, zoning is jurisdiction-depth). None of the nine clears it.

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.finding: I have created a paired-control divergence: TWO checked-in instruments now claim facet 'zoning' with DIFFERENT denominators.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.detail: countyCoverageScoreCli.ts writes facet 'zoning' over the county parcel count; countyRailScoreCli.ts writes it over the incorporated count. Both upsert the same (county_fips, facet) primary key, so the last one run wins the cell: on Bastrop that is 15.22% versus 79.60% depending on which CLI ran most recently.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.disposition: NAMED, NOT RESOLVED. Retiring or re-denominating a live instrument in another lane's file is an operator ruling (DEV_PROCESS 5.4), and countyCoverageScoreCli.ts is SS-W13's. The conflict is written into the registry's zoning note so it cannot be discovered by accident. Neither instrument was applied. OPERATOR RULING REQUESTED.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.label: VERIFIED

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.finding: The corrected denominator is expensive where the old one was free.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.detail: count(DISTINCT feature_index) is a single aggregate; the spatial join is 4m33s on Travis. The cost is bounded only because measurability is resolved BEFORE the join, so only wired counties pay it: 9 counties today, not 254. If wiring grows to hundreds of cities this becomes a real runtime and will need a precomputed parcel-to-city assignment.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.disposition: Stated in the module header rather than discovered later. Backlog candidate, not built here.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.label: VERIFIED

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.finding: The 116 Bastrop and 16,308 Travis parcels outside every boundary are EXCLUDED from the numerator, which lowers the reported number.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.detail: They are real stamps on real parcels. Counting them would be counting a numerator the denominator does not contain. The alternative reading — that tx_city_boundary's 202508 vintage lags the cities' own annexations, so some of those parcels ARE incorporated — is plausible and unestablished.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.disposition: The escape count travels in the provenance detail as `outside=`, so the exclusion is visible at the point of use and a later ruling can act on it. Named as INFERRED, not resolved.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.label: VERIFIED (the counts) / INFERRED (the cause)

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.finding: tx_city_boundary being exactly the incorporated municipalities of Texas is still not POSITIVELY established by me.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.detail: 1,222 rows, source string TxGIO/CPA txgio_city_boundaries_202508, consistent with the roughly 1,220 incorporated Texas municipalities and with the dispatch's figure. I have not verified it against an authoritative roster.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.disposition: Carried forward as an open item rather than asserted. If the table were to include CDPs or ETJs the denominator would be too large and every figure here too low.

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.finding: The envelope facet was deliberately NOT re-denominated.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.detail: envelope is a conjunction of zoning_district AND geometry, measuring whether a deterministic Tier-1 envelope can be DERIVED. That is legitimately a county-wide question: one would want an envelope for a rural parcel too. Its county denominator is correct for its own question, so changing it would have been a blanket edit rather than a measured one.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnWork.disposition: Out of scope by decision, not by omission (DEV_PROCESS 3.3).
